functionDefaultAcl.applicability: The wrapper is created while privacy_workflow_owner is the active owner, so supabase_admin's own public-schema function default ACL does not govern this wrapper.

classification.reason: A PostgreSQL superuser has effective function EXECUTE independently of proacl. Granting EXECUTE to supabase_admin therefore cannot be distinguished with has_function_privilege, although it can add an explicit ACL item.

impactOnFinding.ocr106Acl001Reclassified: The failure demonstrates an undetected explicit ACL grant, not a newly acquired effective privilege.
impactOnFinding.invalidCorrection: Adding has_function_privilege('supabase_admin', ...) as a forbidden effective privilege check would hold the baseline permanently because supabase_admin is a superuser.
validResolutionOptions: If the contract forbids explicit supabase_admin grants, compare the wrapper and helper proacl entries against an exact allowed ACL set and reject an explicit supabase_admin ACL item.
If the contract is only about effective privilege, use a dedicated NOSUPERUSER probe role for the readiness counterexample instead of supabase_admin.

warningEvidence.inference: Because psql advanced beyond GRANT without ON_ERROR_STOP termination but the capability stayed ready, PostgreSQL likely emitted a no-privileges-were-granted warning and made no ACL change.

reclassification.priorOcr106Acl001Outcome: The readiness fixture still failed, but that run does not prove the capability ignored a changed explicit ACL.
reclassification.mostLikelyImmediateCause: The fixture attempted the GRANT with a non-owner actor that could neither inherit nor SET ROLE to privacy_workflow_owner.
reclassification.requiredNextCheck: Run the counterexample under an actor authorized to change the wrapper ACL, preserve the GRANT warning/output, read back proacl before invoking the capability, and only then classify any remaining capability gap.
reclassification.sourceChangeDecision: Do not add a supabase_admin effective-privilege predicate based on this failed run; supabase_admin is a superuser and is always effectively executable.
